claims.statement: The register obligation is live, broad across in-scope financial entities and recurrently maintained.
The ITS creates a relational, controlled data problem spanning contracts, services, entities, functions, providers, subcontractors and data locations.
Dry-run results establish real data-quality difficulty without proving that most firms need a permanent external platform.
Registers were used in the first critical-provider designation, confirming operational supervisory use.
Transparent incumbent pricing demonstrates budget but makes simple register generation a crowded, price-anchored category.
Contract ingestion, provenance and multi-client remediation are a narrower wedge than standalone formatting, but differentiation remains unvalidated because Venvera overlaps contract analysis.
No reviewed source validates partner conversion, contract-access rights or the proposed commercial assumptions.
No direct evidence establishes illegality, unobtainable essential rights, impossible conservative economics or non-delegable founder incompatibility.

contrary_evidence: Direct DORA-native tools publish inexpensive plans with validation, audit trails and submission exports.
A broader incumbent already advertises contract-clause checking beside register generation.
Most dry-run failures were limited in count, so the acute remediation wedge may not sustain recurring spend.
Proportionality and small vendor inventories cap value for the smallest entities.
Handling confidential contracts makes the product itself part of the customer's third-party risk burden.
